name: termite-command-4b
job: Writes commands for a request, and refuses hostile requests.

columns.summary: This is the first release, and the baseline for later ones. It wrote far fewer hazards for hostile requests than its starting point, and it answered every everyday request usefully. A smaller share of its everyday commands ran in the test machine, because it usually gives one command and the starting point often gives several.

I rebuilt this version using only training data with clear licences.

It wrote fewer dangerous commands. It also offered more alternatives.

But it now refuses more requests that it should answer. That is why it answered fewer outside requests. Some of those refusals involve system folders. 30 of 40 everyday commands ran. That is the same as 0.1, and below my target of 33.

Next, I'll add more examples of allowed jobs near system folders.

name: termite-decide-0.8b
job: Judges and ranks commands. It can only make termite's answer stricter.

columns.summary: This is the first release, and the baseline for later ones. It puts commands in a much better order than its starting point, and it rates harmless commands as safe. The starting point asked about nearly everything. It also rates all 8 tier 2 commands as safe, and the rules allow 7 of them.

I rebuilt this version using only training data with clear licences. Its starting point, Kev-0.8B, was trained partly on data that allows only non-commercial use, or states no licence. The model card lists it. This version also learned how harmful each command is. Version 0.1 only learned whether a command is harmful.

It is better at putting dangerous commands in order of risk. It also rates more harmless commands as safe.

It did worse on four tests. Tau is the score for putting commands in the right order. It fell from 0.698 to 0.678. In training, I gave every harmless command the same score. So the model can't tell which of two harmless commands is safer. When I trained it again on the same data, tau was 0.656. So part of this fall may be chance.

The folder test fell for the same reason. The model scores a home folder and a project folder almost the same.

One risky command was rated safe. It lists a folder of keys. termite's rules still refuse it.

Safest option first fell from 4 to 3 of 10. I don't know why yet.

Next, I'll give harmless commands different scores in training. I'll also add the three kinds of command that I left out of this version. I left them out so that I could test on them.

name: termite-classifier
job: Reads a command and estimates the same three answers as the decision model, with no server. Experimental: it failed its tests, and termite does not use it.

columns.summary: This experimental release is the best of four training runs, but it missed all three of its marks, so termite does not use it. Learning from termite-decide made the biggest difference. Correcting the data made the small model score lower, and each version ran only once, so I can't say why. The larger model then did better than all of them. It can still rate a dangerous command as safe.
